key_insight: DVD turns pre-trained video diffusion models into deterministic, single-pass depth regressors by reusing diffusion timesteps as structural anchors and leveraging generative priors to remove stochastic geometric hallucinations and scale drift.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between generative models (which hallucinate geometry and drift in scale) and discriminative models (which need massive labeled datasets to resolve semantic ambiguities), enabling stable, accurate video depth estimation with far less reliance on dense supervision.
method: Deterministic adaptation of pre-trained video diffusion backbones into a single-pass depth regression head.
Repurpose diffusion timesteps as structural anchors/guidance to encode multi-scale geometric cues and stabilize predictions.
Exploit generative priors from the diffusion model to resolve semantic depth ambiguities and suppress stochastic hallucinations, reducing scale drift without heavy labeling.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to get consistent, high-quality video depth maps using generative priors without scaling annotation costs—beneficial for robotics, AR/VR, 3D reconstruction and autonomous systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pre-trained video diffusion model → timestep-based structural anchor → deterministic depth regressor (single pass).
Illustration of 'timestep as anchor': timeline showing diffusion steps informing geometric structure at multiple scales.
Before/after qualitative comparisons: input video frames with depth maps from a generative baseline (hallucinations/scale drift) vs. DVD outputs (stable, consistent depth).
Quantitative chart: depth error and scale-drift curves comparing generative, discriminative, and DVD approaches.
paper_title: DVD: Deterministic Video Depth Estimation with Generative Priors
paper_authors: Hongfei Zhang, Harold Haodong Chen, Chenfei Liao, Jing He, Zixin Zhang
